---
title: "Expanded evidence extraction: preoperative pathology evaluation in prolapse"
format:
  docx:
    toc: true
execute:
  echo: false
---

This extraction supports preliminary model calibration; it is not a
procedure-specific comparative effectiveness estimate. The target population
is asymptomatic postmenopausal women with stage III uterovaginal prolapse.
Published mixed-population studies are labeled as indirect.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-expanded-evidence
#| tbl-cap: "Source-level evidence, including numerator/denominator and applicability"
source_rows <- readr::read_csv(
  "evidence/expanded_screening_extraction_20261109.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
display_rows <- source_rows |>
  dplyr::filter(evidence_class != "missing") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Count = dplyr::if_else(
      !is.na(numerator) & !is.na(denominator),
      paste0(numerator, "/", denominator),
      "—"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    procedure_group, parameter, Count, published_estimate,
    evidence_class, limitations
  )
knitr::kable(display_rows)
```

## Highest-priority unobserved parameters

```{r}
#| label: tbl-critical-gaps
#| tbl-cap: "Missing inputs for decision modeling"
source_rows |>
  dplyr::filter(evidence_class == "missing") |>
  dplyr::select(procedure_group, parameter, limitations) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Rules for using these data

- Use 1/317 for the observed EIN proportion in the asymptomatic
  postmenopausal cohort; do not substitute the 2/106 rate of *combined*
  premalignant/malignant pathology *among patients with polyps*.
- The 8/462 complex atypical hyperplasia estimate comes from a broader POP
  hysterectomy series and is not restricted to postmenopausal patients in the
  reported denominator.
- The 10/30 second-staging estimate is conditional on incidental endometrial
  cancer. Do not apply it to the general prolapse population.
- A 38% complication estimate among selected *inpatient* stump excisions does
  not estimate the probability of complications after SCH itself.
- Future cervix surveillance needs screening eligibility, prior CIN2+/AIS,
  age, and time horizon; screening is not automatically lifelong.
- Keep incident cancer after hysteropexy separate from occult cancer present
  at the index operation; the current model only represents prevalent disease.
- Test performance borrowed from patients with postmenopausal bleeding
  should be sensitivity analyses until validated for asymptomatic patients.
- Do not infer the causal value of earlier detection from survival comparisons
  of patients whose cancer was found before versus after prolapse surgery.

## Interpretation

Current evidence can justify broad sensitivity distributions for occult
endometrial cancer and can inform conditional second-staging probabilities
following unexpected cancer. It is not sufficient to estimate the effect of
routine testing on cancer mortality, the absolute post-hysteropexy diagnostic
delay, or the absolute probability of cervical-stump excision after SCH.
Those missing quantities should remain explicit scenario parameters.

The source URLs and study-specific limitations are retained in the linked CSV
for audit and future manuscript references.
